description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Graduate Software Engineer, Open Source and Linux, Canonical Ubuntu based in United States. 

 We are looking for talented and ambitious graduate software engineers to join globally distributed engineering teams working across open-source technologies and Linux systems. This opportunity is designed for exceptional 2026 and 2027 graduates who are passionate about software engineering and eager to make meaningful contributions to widely used technology platforms. You will work on diverse projects spanning everything from operating systems, kernels, and embedded devices to cloud infrastructure, artificial intelligence, and distributed systems. Depending on your interests and strengths, you will contribute using technologies such as Python, Go, Rust, C/C++, JavaScript, and Java. Working alongside experienced engineers and open-source communities, you will develop your technical expertise through challenging projects, collaborative problem-solving, and continuous learning.



Accountabilities:
 
 Contribute to the design, development, and continuous improvement of open-source software and commercial engineering systems. You will take ownership of meaningful technical challenges while collaborating with globally distributed teams, engaging with users, and developing a deep understanding of Linux and modern software engineering practices.


 
 Contribute to product development and help shape engineering roadmaps during global in-person team sprints held twice a year.



 
 Design and develop intuitive user experiences, including developer tools, command-line applications, and software interfaces.



 
 Write high-quality, reliable, secure, and performant code for products and services potentially used by millions of people worldwide.



 
 Develop technical expertise and progressively master key programming languages, software engineering practices, and Linux system technologies.



 
 Engage with open-source communities and users through code reviews, issue trackers, and collaborative development activities.



 
 Respond to customer issues and technical challenges, prioritizing effective solutions and developing an understanding of enterprise requirements.



 
 Apply security-conscious engineering principles throughout software design, development, and implementation.



 
 Collaborate with colleagues across different regions and technical disciplines through remote teamwork, pair programming, mentoring, and shared problem-solving.



 
 Participate in engineering discussions and contribute ideas that improve product quality, performance, usability, and long-term maintainability.



 
 Explore different engineering domains and technologies, potentially including kernels, drivers, cloud computing, containers, Kubernetes, embedded Linux, AI/ML, data science, and distributed systems.



 
 Contribute to technical documentation and knowledge sharing within engineering teams and the wider open-source ecosystem.




 Requirements :

 The ideal candidate is an academically high-performing graduate with strong programming fundamentals, a genuine passion for open-source technologies, and the motivation to tackle complex engineering challenges. You should demonstrate curiosity, initiative, accountability, and the ability to work independently while contributing effectively to an international engineering team.


 
 Bachelor's degree completed or expected in 2026 or 2027 in Computer Science, Business Informatics, Mathematics, or another STEM discipline that includes programming coursework.



 
 Exceptional academic performance throughout high school and university, supported by strong results or recognized academic achievements.



 
 Confidence in developing and delivering high-quality software using at least one of the following languages: Python, Rust, C, C++, Go, JavaScript, or Java.



 
 Practical experience with Ubuntu or another Linux distribution.



 
 Personal technology or software engineering projects completed outside academic coursework or professional employment.



 
 Strong understanding of programming fundamentals and enthusiasm for learning complex software systems.



 
 Excellent written and spoken English.



 
 Strong interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to collaborate across international and distributed teams.



 
 A results-oriented and organized approach, with the motivation to meet commitments and deliver high-quality outcomes.



 
 Curiosity, flexibility, personal accountability, and a willingness to take ownership of responsibilities.



 
 Self-awareness, thoughtful decision-making, and the ability to reflect on feedback and continuously improve.



 
 Willingness and ability to travel internationally two to four times per year for company events lasting approximately one to two weeks.




 Nice-to-have qualifications:


 
 Previous contributions to upstream open-source projects.



 
 Experience with software packaging or Linux distributions such as Debian, Fedora, Arch, or Nix.



 
 Leadership, organizational, or team coordination experience.



 
 Strong presentation, technical writing, and documentation skills.



 
 Interest in business, commercial technology, and the relationship between open-source software and enterprise solutions.




 Benefits: 


 
 Fully remote, globally distributed working environment.



 
 Opportunities to collaborate in person during twice-yearly engineering sprints.



 
 Annual personal learning and development budget of USD 2,000.



 
 Biannual compensation and performance reviews.



 
 Performance-driven annual bonus or commission opportunities.



 
 Company recognition and rewards programs.



 
 40 days of annual leave, including public holidays and company-wide holiday periods.



 
 Maternity and paternity leave.



 
 Access to a Team Member Assistance Program and wellness platform.



 
 International travel opportunities to meet colleagues and collaborate with engineering teams.



 
 Priority Pass lounge access for eligible business travel.



 
 Opportunities to work on impactful open-source projects and develop expertise across a broad range of technologies.



 
 Long-term professional development through mentorship, technical collaboration, and exposure to global engineering challenges.






How Jobgether works:
